body.heading: Find flat pebbles
paragraphs: Look for smooth, flat pebbles. Flat stones stack best because they give the next stone a steady place to sit.
Start with the biggest, flattest pebble at the bottom. A tower is only as strong as its first stone.

body.heading: Stack slowly
paragraphs: Add one pebble at a time. Before you let go, feel whether it wobbles. If it wobbles, turn it around or choose a different stone.
Small stones can fill gaps and steady a wobbly layer. Builders of real stone walls use exactly this trick.

body.heading: Count your tower
paragraphs: How many pebbles high can you go? Count them before the tower tumbles — and it will tumble, which is part of the fun.
Try again with a wider bottom stone. Each fall teaches your hands something new about balance.

takeaway: Tall pebble towers need a wide, flat start and patient hands — every tumble teaches you balance.
safetyNotes: Only stack pebbles you can lift easily — never drop stones on toes. Wash your hands after handling beach pebbles, and gently take your tower down when you finish.
screenFreeExtension: Build a tower of cushions or wooden blocks indoors and try to beat your pebble record.
